parsed.rationale: Although `PlaybackController` and `TimeShiftablePlayer` share four members (`installRenderTap:()`, `removeRenderTap:()`, `isPlaying:Bool`, and `makeAudioBufferStream:() -> AsyncStream<AVAudioPCMBuffer>`), the structural evidence explicitly records `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, indicating the pipeline itself found no meaningful overlap. More importantly, the two protocols encode distinct domain responsibilities: `PlaybackController` models high-level playback control with `PlaybackState`, `PlaybackReason`-parameterised `play`/`stop`/`toggle`, and a loading indicator, while `TimeShiftablePlayer` models a lower-level, time-shifting audio player with `seek`, `seekToLive`, `secondsBehindLive`, `maxLookbackSeconds`, and multiple async event/state streams typed differently (`PlayerState` vs `PlaybackState`). Forcing an inheritance relationship would either leak time-shifting concerns into the general controller abstraction or require a vacuous base protocol so thin it adds no value. The coincidence of four shared method names reflects the shared audio-playback domain, not a refactorable structural duplication.
